questions.knowledge_point: Finding the Amplitude for the Amplitude-Phase Form for Sine
questions.worked_solution:
The sum formula for sine gives

$$
\begin{aligned}R\operatorname{sin}⁡(x+ϕ) & =R(\operatorname{sin}⁡x\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ+\operatorname{cos}⁡x\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ) \\  & =R\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ\operatorname{sin}⁡x+R\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ\operatorname{cos}⁡x.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, by writing the given expression in the amplitude-phase form

$$
6\operatorname{sin}⁡x+8\operatorname{cos}⁡x=R\operatorname{sin}⁡(x+ϕ),
$$

we get the following identity:

$$
6\operatorname{sin}⁡x+8\operatorname{cos}⁡x=(R\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ)\operatorname{sin}⁡x+(R\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ)\operatorname{cos}⁡x
$$

Equating the coefficients of $\operatorname{sin}⁡x$ and $\operatorname{cos}⁡x,$ we get the following system of equations:

$$
{\begin{aligned}R\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ=6 \\ R\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ=8\end{aligned}
$$

Squaring the first and the second equations of the system and adding the results together, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{(R\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ)}^{2}+{(R\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ)}^{2} & ={6}^{2}+{8}^{2} \\ {R}^{2}({cos}^{2}⁡ϕ+{sin}^{2}⁡ϕ) & =36+64 \\ {R}^{2} & =100 \\ R & =10.\end{aligned}
$$

Note that we only consider the positive root since $R>0.$

questions.problem: Given that the expression $4\operatorname{sin}⁡x-\operatorname{cos}⁡x$ can be written as $R\operatorname{sin}⁡(x-ϕ)$ with $R>0,$ what is the value of $R?$
questions.worked_solution:
The difference formula for sine gives

$$
\begin{aligned}R\operatorname{sin}⁡(x-ϕ) & =R(\operatorname{sin}⁡x\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ-\operatorname{cos}⁡x\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ) \\  & =R\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ\operatorname{sin}⁡x-R\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ\operatorname{cos}⁡x.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, by writing the given expression in the amplitude-phase form

$$
4\operatorname{sin}⁡x-\operatorname{cos}⁡x=R\operatorname{sin}⁡(x-ϕ),
$$

we get the following identity:

$$
4\operatorname{sin}⁡x-\operatorname{cos}⁡x=(R\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ)\operatorname{sin}⁡x-(R\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ)\operatorname{cos}⁡x
$$

Equating the coefficients of $\operatorname{sin}⁡x$ and $\operatorname{cos}⁡x,$ we get the following system of equations:

$$
{\begin{aligned}R\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ=4 \\ R\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ=1\end{aligned}
$$

Squaring the first and the second equations of the system and adding the results together, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{(R\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ)}^{2}+{(R\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ)}^{2} & ={4}^{2}+{1}^{2} \\ {R}^{2}({cos}^{2}⁡ϕ+{sin}^{2}⁡ϕ) & =16+1 \\ {R}^{2} & =17 \\ R & =\sqrt{17}.\end{aligned}
$$

Note that we only consider the positive root since $R>0.$

Express $2\operatorname{sin}⁡(4x)+2\operatorname{cos}⁡(4x)$ in the form $R\operatorname{sin}⁡(4x+ϕ)$ with $ϕ\in (0,{90}^{∘}).$

$2\operatorname{sin}⁡(4x)+2\operatorname{cos}⁡(4x)=$
 {{field-1}}
$\operatorname{sin}⁡(4x\,+$
{{field-2}}${}^{∘})$
questions.worked_solution:
The sum formula for sine gives

$$
\begin{aligned}R\operatorname{sin}⁡(4x+ϕ) & =R(\operatorname{sin}⁡(4x)\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ+\operatorname{cos}⁡(4x)\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ) \\  & =R\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ\operatorname{sin}⁡(4x)+R\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ\operatorname{cos}⁡(4x).\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, by writing the given expression in the amplitude-phase form

$$
2\operatorname{sin}⁡(4x)+2\operatorname{cos}⁡(4x)=R\operatorname{sin}⁡(4x+ϕ),
$$

we get the following identity:

$$
2\operatorname{sin}⁡(4x)+2\operatorname{cos}⁡(4x)=(R\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ)\operatorname{sin}⁡(4x)+(R\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ)\operatorname{cos}⁡(4x)
$$

Equating the coefficients of $\operatorname{sin}⁡(4x)$ and $\operatorname{cos}⁡(4x),$ we get the following system of equations:

$$
{\begin{aligned}R\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ=2 \\ R\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ=2\end{aligned}
$$

Dividing the second equation by the first, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{R\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ}{R\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ} & =\frac{2}{2} \\ \operatorname{tan}⁡ϕ & =1 \\ ϕ & =\operatorname{arctan}⁡(1) \\  & ={45}^{∘}.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we find the amplitude $R.$ Squaring the first and the second equations of the system and adding the results together, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{(R\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ)}^{2}+{(R\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ)}^{2} & ={2}^{2}+{2}^{2} \\ {R}^{2}({cos}^{2}⁡ϕ+{sin}^{2}⁡ϕ) & =4+4 \\ {R}^{2} & =8 \\ R & =2\sqrt{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Note that we only consider the positive root since $R>0.$

Finally, we can write the initial expression in amplitude-phase form as follows:

$$
2\operatorname{sin}⁡(4x)+2\operatorname{cos}⁡(4x)=2\sqrt{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡(4x+{45}^{∘})
$$

questions.problem: $4\operatorname{sin}⁡x+3\operatorname{cos}⁡x≈$
questions.worked_solution:
The sum formula for sine gives

$$
\begin{aligned}R\operatorname{sin}⁡(x+ϕ) & =R(\operatorname{sin}⁡x\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ+\operatorname{cos}⁡x\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ) \\  & =R\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ\operatorname{sin}⁡x+R\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ\operatorname{cos}⁡x.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, by writing the given expression in the amplitude-phase form

$$
4\operatorname{sin}⁡x+3\operatorname{cos}⁡x=R\operatorname{sin}⁡(x+ϕ),
$$

we get the following identity:

$$
4\operatorname{sin}⁡x+3\operatorname{cos}⁡x=(R\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ)\operatorname{sin}⁡x+(R\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ)\operatorname{cos}⁡x
$$

Equating the coefficients of $\operatorname{sin}⁡x$ and $\operatorname{cos}⁡x,$ we get the following system of equations:

$$
{\begin{aligned}R\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ=4 \\ R\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ=3\end{aligned}
$$

Dividing the second equation by the first, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{R\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ}{R\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ} & =\frac{3}{4} \\ \operatorname{tan}⁡ϕ & =\frac{3}{4} \\ ϕ & =\operatorname{arctan}⁡(\frac{3}{4}) \\ ϕ & ≈0.644\,\text{rad}\end{aligned}
$$

rounded to three decimal places.

Now, we find the amplitude $R.$ Squaring the first and the second equations of the system and adding the results together, we get: 

$$
\begin{aligned}{R}^{2}{sin}^{2}⁡ϕ+{R}^{2}{cos}^{2}⁡ϕ & ={3}^{2}+{4}^{2} \\ {R}^{2}({sin}^{2}⁡ϕ+{cos}^{2}⁡ϕ) & =9+16 \\ {R}^{2} & =25 \\ R & =5\end{aligned}
$$

Note that we only consider the positive root since $R>0.$

Finally, we can write the initial expression in amplitude-phase form as follows:

$$
4\operatorname{sin}⁡x+3\operatorname{cos}⁡x≈5\operatorname{sin}⁡(x+0.644)
$$

questions.problem: Given that the expression $2\operatorname{sin}⁡x+3\operatorname{cos}⁡x$ can be written as $R\operatorname{cos}⁡(x-ϕ)$ with $R>0$, what is the value of $R?$
questions.worked_solution:
The difference formula for cosine gives

$$
\begin{aligned}R\operatorname{cos}⁡(x-ϕ) & =R(\operatorname{cos}⁡(x)\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ+\operatorname{sin}⁡(x)\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ) \\  & =R\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ\operatorname{cos}⁡(x)+R\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ\operatorname{sin}⁡(x)\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, by writing the given expression in the amplitude-phase form

$$
2\operatorname{sin}⁡x+3\operatorname{cos}⁡x=R\operatorname{cos}⁡(x-ϕ),
$$

we get the following identity:

$$
2\operatorname{sin}⁡x+3\operatorname{cos}⁡x=(R\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ)\operatorname{sin}⁡x+(R\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ)\operatorname{cos}⁡x
$$

Equating the coefficients of $\operatorname{sin}⁡x$ and $\operatorname{cos}⁡x,$ we get the following system of equations:

$$
{\begin{aligned}R\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ=3 \\ R\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ=2\end{aligned}
$$

Squaring the first and the second equations of the system and adding the results together, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{(R\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ)}^{2}+{(R\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ)}^{2} & =(2)^{2}+(3)^{2} \\ {R}^{2}({sin}^{2}⁡ϕ+{cos}^{2}⁡ϕ) & =4+9 \\ {R}^{2} & =13 \\ R & =\sqrt{13}\end{aligned}
$$

Note that we only consider the positive root since $R>0.$

$$
\sqrt{5}\operatorname{sin}⁡(6x)+4\operatorname{cos}⁡(6x)=R\operatorname{cos}⁡(6x-ϕ),

$$
\sqrt{5}\operatorname{sin}⁡(6x)+4\operatorname{cos}⁡(6x)=(R\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ)\operatorname{sin}⁡(6x)+(R\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ)\operatorname{cos}⁡(6x).

canonical_examples.problem: Given that the expression $\sqrt{2}\sin x + \sqrt{7}\cos x$ can be written as $R\sin(x+\phi)$ with $R>0,$ what is the value of $R?$
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
The sum formula for sine gives

$$
\begin{aligned}R\operatorname{sin}⁡(x+ϕ) & =R(\operatorname{sin}⁡x\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ+\operatorname{cos}⁡x\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ) \\  & =R\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ\operatorname{sin}⁡x+R\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ\operatorname{cos}⁡x.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, by writing the given expression in the amplitude-phase form

$$
\sqrt{2}\sin x + \sqrt{7}\cos x   = R\sin(x+\phi),
$$

we get the following identity:

$$
\sqrt{2}\sin x + \sqrt{7}\cos x    = (R \cos \phi ) \sin x + (R \sin \phi ) \cos x
$$

Equating the coefficients of $\sin x$ and $\cos x,$ we have the following system:

$$
{\begin{aligned}R\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ=\sqrt{2} \\ R\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ=\sqrt{7}\end{aligned}
$$

Squaring the first and the second equations of the system and adding the results together, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{(R\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ)}^{2}+{(R\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ)}^{2} & ={\sqrt{2}}^{2}+{\sqrt{7}}^{2} \\ {R}^{2}({cos}^{2}⁡ϕ+{sin}^{2}⁡ϕ) & =2+7 \\ {R}^{2} & =9 \\ R & =3.\end{aligned}
$$

Note that we only consider the positive root since $R>0.$

2 \sin x - 2 \cos x = R\sin(x-\phi),
